He is also part of an ownership group that purchased the [[Baltimore Orioles]] in 2024. Hill also works as a basketball analyst for [[CBS Sports|CBS]], [[NBC Sports|NBC]] and [[TNT Sports (United States)|Turner Sports]].{{Cite web |last=Rapp |first=Timothy |date=February 1, 2024 |title=Cal Ripken Jr., Grant Hill Part of New Orioles Ownership Group Led by Rubenstein |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10107446-cal-ripken-jr-grant-hill-part-of-new-orioles-ownership-group-led-by-rubenstein |website=[[Bleacher Report]]}} A four-year player at [[Duke University]], Hill was touted as one of the greatest [[college basketball]] players ever. In the NBA, he played for the [[Detroit Pistons]], the [[Orlando Magic]], the [[Phoenix Suns]], and the [[Los Angeles Clippers]], mostly at the [[small forward]] position. Hill is a seven-time [[NBA All-Star Game|NBA All-Star]], a five-time [[All-NBA]] selection, and a three-time winner of the [[NBA Sportsmanship Award]]. In 2018, he was inducted into the [[Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame]]. The 1994 [[Atlantic Coast Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|ACC Player of the Year]], a two-time [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|NCAA All-American]], and a two-time [[List of NCAA Men's Division I Basketball champions|NCAA champion]], Hill is generally considered one of the best ever to play for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]]. After graduating in 1994, Hill was selected by the Pistons with the third overall pick in the [[1994 NBA draft|NBA draft]]. He was the co-winner of the 1995 [[NBA Rookie of the Year Award]] with [[Jason Kidd]]. Early in his NBA career, Hill was widely considered one of the best all-around players in the game, often leading his team in points, [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] and [[assist (basketball)|assists]]. In his first six seasons in the NBA, Hill averaged 21.6 points, 7.9 rebounds, and 6.3 assists per game and made the Eastern Conference All-Star Team five times. An ankle injury in 2000 changed the trajectory of his career. It plagued him for several years, led to a March 2003 surgery that was followed by life-threatening complications, and forced him to miss the entire 2003–04 season. In 2005, Hill made the Eastern Conference All-Star Team as a member of the Magic. He played in the Western Conference Finals in 2010 with the Phoenix Suns. In the 12 seasons after his ankle injury, Hill averaged 13.1 points, 4.7 rebounds, and 2.6 assists per game. On June 1, 2013, Hill announced his retirement from the NBA. In 2015, Hill and [[Tony Ressler]] were part of an ownership group that purchased the [[Atlanta Hawks]]. In 2023, Hill and his wife, [[Tamia]] became part owners of [[Major League Soccer|MLS]] club [[Orlando City SC|Orlando City]] and [[National Women's Soccer League|NWSL]] club, [[Orlando Pride]].{{Cite web |last=orlandocitysc |title=Orlando Icons Tamia and Grant Hill Join Orlando City SC and Orlando Pride Ownership Group {{!}} Orlando City |url=https://www.orlandocitysc.com/news/orlando-icons-tamia-and-grant-hill-join-orlando-city-sc-and-orlando-pride-owners |access-date=2023-10-27 |website=orlandocitysc |language=en}}

'''Gary Dwayne Payton Sr.'''<ref name=br>{{cite basketball-reference|id=p/paytoga01|accessdate=September 10, 2024}}</ref> (born July 23, 1968) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who played in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) for 17 seasons. Nicknamed "'''the Glove'''" for his defensive abilities, he is widely regarded as one of the greatest [[point guard|point guards]] of all time. He spent the majority of his career with the [[Seattle SuperSonics]], where he holds franchise records in [[assist (basketball)|assists]] and [[steal (basketball)|steals]], and later played short stints for the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], [[Los Angeles Lakers]], [[Boston Celtics]], and [[Miami Heat]]. He made three [[NBA Finals]] appearances: with the Sonics in [[1996 NBA Finals|1996]], the Lakers in [[2004 NBA Finals|2004]], and the Heat in [[2006 NBA Finals|2006]], winning in the last.

Payton was the first (and, until [[Marcus Smart]] was selected in 2022, only) point guard to win the [[NBA Defensive Player of the Year]] award.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://dimemag.com/2007/10/hall-of-fame-watch-gary-payton/ |title=The H.O.F. Watch – Gary Payton |publisher=Dimemag.com |date=October 4, 2007 |access-date=September 21, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100718001246/http://dimemag.com/2007/10/hall-of-fame-watch-gary-payton/ |archive-date=July 18, 2010 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/dailydime?page=dailydime-GreatestPointGuards |title=10 greatest point guards ever |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=May 11, 2006 |access-date=September 21, 2010}}</ref> He was selected for nine [[All-NBA Team]]s, [[NBA All-Defensive Team|All-Defensive First Team]]s (tying the record)<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 9, 2011 |title=NBA announces all-defensive team |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=6516619 |access-date=May 9, 2011 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}}</ref>, and [[NBA All-Star Game|All-Star Games]] each. He was inducted into the [[Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame]] in 2013<ref>[http://www.cbssports.com/nba/eye-on-basketball/23544934/video-gary-paytons-hall-of-fame-induction-video-and-speech Gary Payton's Hall of Fame induction video and speech]</ref> and named to the [[NBA 75th Anniversary Team]]<ref>{{cite web |title=NBA's 75 Anniversary Team Players |url=https://www.nba.com/75 |website=NBA.com |access-date=January 4, 2022}}</ref> in 2021.

'''Glenn Alan Robinson Jr.''' (born January 10, 1973) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. Nicknamed "'''Big Dog'''" and "'''the Chosen One'''",<ref>{{cite web|title=Glenn Robinson Stats|website=Basketball-Reference.com|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/r/robingl01.html|access-date=August 2, 2021|archive-date=February 24, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110224144121/http://www.basketball-reference.com/players/r/robingl01.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Glenn Robinson Theodore Roosevelt High School Sport: Basketball |url=https://garysportshalloffame.org/inductees/glenn-robinson/ |website=Gary Sports Hall of Fame |access-date=July 24, 2022 |archive-date=February 9, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230209140844/https://garysportshalloffame.org/inductees/glenn-robinson/ |url-status=live }}</ref> he played in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) from 1994 to 2005 for the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], [[Atlanta Hawks]], [[Philadelphia 76ers]], and [[San Antonio Spurs]]. Robinson attended [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue University]] and was the first overall pick in the [[1994 NBA draft]]. He is the father of [[Glenn Robinson III]], who played college basketball at the [[University of Michigan]] and has also played in the NBA. His daughter is [[Jaimie Robinson]].

Arenas was nicknamed "'''Agent Zero'''" while playing with Washington, due to his jersey number (0).<ref name="McKenna 2010">{{cite web|url=http://www.washingtoncitypaper.com/display.php?id=38336 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120919052034/http://www.washingtoncitypaper.com/display.php?id=38336 |url-status=dead |archive-date=September 19, 2012 |title=Arenas: Agent Zero to Agent of Misfortune |last=McKenna |first=Dave |newspaper=[[Washington City Paper]] |date=January 15, 2010 |access-date=September 23, 2010 }}</ref> He was also nicknamed "'''[[Shichirin|Hibachi]]'''" for "cooking" his opponents. Both names quickly became fan favorites during his time in the Washington, D.C. area.<ref>''[[Slam (magazine)|SLAM]]'' (December 2006). "Issue 103, pg. 26".</ref> Arenas played the [[point guard]] and [[shooting guard]] positions.

'''Goran Dragić''' (born 6 May 1986) is a Slovenian former professional [[basketball]] player. He was an [[All-NBA Third Team]] selection and the [[NBA Most Improved Player Award|NBA Most Improved Player]] with the Suns in 2014. He was named an [[NBA All-Star]] for the first time in 2018 with Miami. 

Internationally, Dragić led the senior [[Slovenian national basketball team|Slovenian national team]] to its first [[FIBA EuroBasket]] title in [[EuroBasket 2017|2017]], while being named the [[FIBA EuroBasket MVP|MVP of the tournament]]. He is second in all-time points scored for the team and has played ninety games for his country.

'''Gordon Daniel Hayward''' (born March 23, 1990) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played 14 seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) for the [[Utah Jazz]], [[Boston Celtics]], [[Charlotte Hornets]], and [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].

In [[college basketball]], Hayward led the [[Butler Bulldogs men's basketball|Butler Bulldogs]] to the [[2010 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Championship Game|championship game]] of the [[2010 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2010 NCAA tournament]]. He was subsequently selected by the Utah Jazz with the ninth overall pick of the [[2010 NBA draft]]. Hayward played seven seasons with the Jazz, and was selected to the [[2017 NBA All-Star Game]]. In the 2017 offseason, Hayward signed as a free agent with the Celtics, but was ruled out for the remainder of the [[2017–18 NBA season|2017–18 season]] after suffering a fractured [[tibia]] and dislocated ankle only five minutes into the season opener. He played two more seasons with the franchise before the Celtics traded Hayward to the Hornets in a sign-and-trade agreement in November 2020.

'''Glenn Alann ‘Tre’ Robinson III''' (born January 8, 1994) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Sharjah SC (basketball)|Sharjah SC]] of the [[UAE National Basketball League]]. He was drafted 40th overall by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] in the [[2014 NBA draft]]. He played nine seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) for the Timberwolves, [[Philadelphia 76ers]], [[Indiana Pacers]], [[Detroit Pistons]], [[Golden State Warriors]] and [[Sacramento Kings]]. Robinson won the [[Slam Dunk Contest|NBA Slam Dunk Contest]] in 2017.

He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan Wolverines]], where he was an All-Freshman team honoree in during the [[2012–13 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season]] for the [[2012–13 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2012–13 Michigan Wolverines team]] that finished as [[2013 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship Game|national runner-up]] in the [[2013 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]]. He returned to play for the [[2013–14 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season]] champion [[2013–14 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2013–14 Wolverines]] before departing for the NBA.

Robinson was an all-state high school basketball player for [[Lake Central High School]] in [[St. John, Indiana]]. He is the son of [[Glenn Robinson]], the 1994 [[List of first overall NBA draft picks|first overall NBA draft pick]]. Two of his siblings were multiple time state champions in high school in individual events.

Born and raised in [[Athens]] to [[Nigerians|Nigerian]] parents, Antetokounmpo began playing basketball for the youth teams of [[EFAO Zografou B.C.|Filathlitikos]] in Athens. In 2011, he began playing for the club's senior team before entering the [[2013 NBA draft]], where he was selected 15th overall by the Bucks. In [[2016–17 Milwaukee Bucks season|2016–17]], he led the Bucks in all five major statistical categories and became the first player in NBA history to finish a regular season in the top 20 in all five statistics: total points, rebounds, assists, steals, and blocks.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/article/2017/04/12/giannis-antetokounmpo-leads-milwaukee-bucks-five-major-statistical-categories |title=Milwaukee Bucks superstar Giannis Antetokounmpo finishes breakout season in league of his own |work=NBA.com |date=April 12, 2017 |access-date=April 13, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170414001717/http://www.nba.com/article/2017/04/12/giannis-antetokounmpo-leads-milwaukee-bucks-five-major-statistical-categories |archive-date=April 14, 2017 |url-status=live}}</ref> He received the [[NBA Most Improved Player]] award in 2017. Antetokounmpo has received ten [[NBA All-Star]] selections, including being selected as an All-Star [[Captain (sports)|captain]] in 2019, 2020, 2023, and 2024 as he led the [[Eastern Conference (NBA)|Eastern Conference]] in voting in these four years.

One of the most decorated players in NBA history,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3073534/2022/01/18/nba-75-at-no-24-giannis-antetokounmpo-has-become-one-of-the-games-most-decorated-players-in-less-than-a-decade/ |title=NBA 75: At No. 24, Giannis Antetokounmpo has become one of the game's most decorated players in less than a decade – The Athletic |publisher=Theathletic.com |date=January 18, 2022 |access-date=February 15, 2022 |archive-date=March 7, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220307052121/https://theathletic.com/3073534/2022/01/18/nba-75-at-no-24-giannis-antetokounmpo-has-become-one-of-the-games-most-decorated-players-in-less-than-a-decade/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Antetokounmpo won consecutive [[NBA Most Valuable Player]] (MVP) awards in 2019 and 2020, joining [[Kareem Abdul-Jabbar]] and [[LeBron James]] as the only players in NBA history to win two MVPs before turning 26. Along with his second MVP award, he was named the [[NBA Defensive Player of the Year]] in 2020, becoming only the third player, after [[Michael Jordan]] (1988) and [[Hakeem Olajuwon]] (1994), to win both awards in the same season. Antetokounmpo is a nine [[All-NBA Team|All-NBA Team]] member (including seven first-team selections). In [[2021 NBA Finals|2021]], he led the Bucks to their first [[List of NBA champions|NBA championship]] since [[1971 NBA Finals|1971]] and was named [[NBA Finals Most Valuable Player Award|Finals MVP]].<ref name="freak">{{cite web |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/giannis-antetokounmpo-wins-2021-nba-finals-mvp-bucks-star-becomes-youngest-winner-since-kawhi-leonard-in-2014/ |title=Giannis Antetokounmpo wins 2021 NBA Finals MVP |website=CBS Sports |last=Quinn |first=Sam |date=July 21, 2021 |access-date=July 21, 2021 |archive-date=July 23, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210723031121/https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/giannis-antetokounmpo-wins-2021-nba-finals-mvp-bucks-star-becomes-youngest-winner-since-kawhi-leonard-in-2014/ |url-status=live}}</ref> The same year, Antetokounmpo was honored as one of the league's greatest players of all time by being named to the [[NBA 75th Anniversary Team]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/news/nba-75th-anniversary-team-announced |title=NBA 75th Anniversary Team announced |date=October 21, 2021 |website=NBA.com |access-date=November 5, 2021 |archive-date=October 22, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211022003548/https://www.nba.com/news/nba-75th-anniversary-team-announced |url-status=live}}</ref>

Antetokounmpo was named one of ''[[Time 100|Time]]''{{'}}s 100 most influential people in the world in 2021 and has been listed by ''[[Forbes]]'' as one of the [[Forbes list of the world's highest-paid athletes|world's ten highest-paid athletes]] in 2022 and 2024.

For his sporting achievements in his discipline, on July 10, 2024, the [[Hellenic Olympic Committee]] designated him as the Greek flag bearer for the [[2024 Summer Olympics|Paris 2024 Olympic Games]], along with [[Race walking|race walker]] [[Antigoni Drisbioti]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.anocolympic.org/noc-highlights/greeces-flagbearers-for-paris-olympics-announced/#:~:text=The%20Plenary%20Session%20of%20the,the%20Paris%202024%20Olympic%20Games. |title=GREECE'S FLAGBEARERS FOR PARIS OLYMPICS ANNOUNCED |publisher=Greek Olympic Committee |language=EN |date=July 11, 2024 |access-date=July 11, 2024}}</ref> The film ''[[Rise (2022 American film)|Rise]]'', based on the life of Antetokounmpo and his family, was released in 2022.
